newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Wall Street rise boosts Brazil shares at the close.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street rise boosts Brazil shares at the close.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended firm in higher turnover on Friday as a surge in the Dow Industrials brought optimism to the local market, brokers said.
"Activity in New York set the tone of the market here," said a senior trader, noting domestic share prices fluctuated in tandem with the Dow.
The Bovespa index closed up 733 points at 64,643 points, a rise of 1.15 percent.
Volume rose 64 percent to 502.6 million reais ($493.5 million), the highest so far this month, on an increase of local and foreign buy orders.
Analysts said stocks may keep rising next week as Wall Street share prices continue to show strength.
"No key political decisions are expected for the week, so firmness on Wall Street is likely to bolster the market," another trader said.
Bellwether Telebras preferred increased 1.78 percent, ending at 79.75 reais, while its common stock rose 1.95 percent to close at 64.69 reais.
State power utility Eletrobras jumped 2.16 percent to 284 reais, following news that the privatization of Eletrobras' major assets will begin by the end of 1997.

Jose Pio Borges, vice-president and privatization chief at Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), said today Eletrobras minority shareholders will be able to swap their stake for shares in the privatized units.
"This also helped to boost the stock," one said, adding analysts had been concerned about the future of Eletrobras holders in light of the privatization.
Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index (IEE), comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the sector, rose 1.0 percent, closing at 1,609 points.
